summary: The audit checks 25 units of letter-graded GERMAN courses numbered 200 or above, all taken at Stanford. Faculty expect a B+ or better and review lower grades, which the audit does not treat as failing.

program.why: Grading: "PhD students in the department must take required courses for a letter grade if available"; the minor's rule asks for "letter-graded GERMAN courses". The B+ is an expectation that faculty review, not a floor.

y6IHhpUQ.why: "Students must complete a minimum of 25 units of letter-graded GERMAN courses at the 200+ level." Every course in the minor is letter graded, so that is program-wide too.
